The following text is from William Carlos Williams's 1925 creative nonfiction book [i]In the American Grain[/i]. Williams is discussing how works by nineteenth-century US poet and fiction writer Edgar Allan Poe were received by American readers.

Poe must suffer by his originality. Invent that which is new, even if it be made of pine from your own yard, and there's none to know what you have done. It is because there's no name. This is the cause of Poe's lack of recognition. He was American. He was the astounding, inconceivable growth of his locality. Gape at him they did, and he at them in amazement. Afterward with mutual hatred; he in disgust, they in mistrust. It is only that which is under your nose, that which has been named before, that the American reader can take to his bosom. Poe was not a fault of nature, a find for French eyes, ripe but unaccountable, as through our woolyheadedness we've sought to designate him, but a genius intimately shaped by his locality and time. questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
● Louis Ballard was a classical composer and citizen of the Quapaw Tribe.
● His works blend Western classical music with elements of various Native musical traditions.
● His 1970 composition [i]Cacéga Ayuwípi[/i] incorporates a Pueblo water drum, a traditional Native instrument.
● Critic Peter Altman commended Ballard's ability to synthesize "strong, idiomatically modern expressions."
questions.prompt: The student wants to present Altman's claim to an audience already familiar with Louis Ballard. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ballard was commended for his musical compositions, many of which blend Western classical music with elements of various Native musical traditions, by the critic Peter Altman.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ballard's works demonstrate what Peter Altman refers to as an ability to synthesize "strong, idiomatically modern expressions."

choices.label: C
choices.text: Peter Altman praised Ballard—a classical composer whose works blend Western classical music with elements of Native musical traditions—for creating "strong, idiomatically modern expressions."

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ballard's 1970 [i]Cacéga Ayuwípi[/i] blends Western classical music and elements of various Native musical traditions by incorporating a Pueblo water drum.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
● A nonnative species is considered invasive if it causes environmental or economic harm in an ecosystem.
● Curly pondweed is a species of aquatic plant native to parts of Eurasia.
● It can also be found in the northern and western US.
● There, it crowds out native plants and impedes aquatic recreation.
● It is considered an invasive species in the US.
questions.prompt: The student wants to provide an example of an invasive species. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: In the northern and western US, curly pondweed is an invasive aquatic plant that crowds out native plants and impedes aquatic recreation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: One way a nonnative species of plant could cause harm in an ecosystem is by crowding out native plants and impeding aquatic recreation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A nonnative species that crowds out native plants and impedes aquatic recreation, causing environmental or economic harm, is considered invasive.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Curly pondweed is an example of an invasive species that causes environmental or economic harm in parts of Eurasia.
